international.headline: United States and Jordan conduct the 12th Eager Lion exercise
facts: The 12th Eager Lion exercise began at Fort Carson, Colorado, on 15 September 2026, with more than 200 personnel from the United States and Jordan participating.
The two-week biennial exercise was conducted by US Central Command and the Jordanian Armed Forces.
Its focus areas included counter-terrorism, air defence, maritime security, cyber operations and disaster response across land, air, maritime and cyber domains.
The notes state that the United States hosted the exercise for the first time in 2026.
international.summary: Eager Lion 2026 was a biennial US-Jordan exercise focused on coordination across several operational domains.
international.staticLink: US CENTCOM was established in 1983 and is headquartered at MacDill Air Force Base, Florida.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Exercise: Eager Lion; edition: 12th; participating countries: United States and Jordan; venue: Fort Carson, Colorado.
international.mainsAngle: Multidomain exercises can develop interoperability and coordination for security and disaster-response tasks.

national.headline: India hosts the World Circular Economy Forum in Gandhinagar
facts: The 10th World Circular Economy Forum was held at Mahatma Mandir Convention Centre, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, from September 15–18, 2026.
The theme was “Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity”; the notes identify it as the first WCEF held in South Asia.
The forum seeks to accelerate movement from a linear take-make-waste model to a regenerative circular economy through policy, business innovation and cross-sector cooperation.
Discussion areas included market transformation, Global South partnerships, private investment, circular finance and scalable solutions.
The forum was launched in 2017 through an initiative of Sitra, the Finnish Innovation Fund.
national.summary: The forum promoted circular-economy policies and business approaches intended to keep resources in use and reduce waste.
national.staticLink: Circular-economy principles listed in the notes include reducing, reusing, repairing, recycling and recovering.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The 10th WCEF was hosted in Gandhinagar and was the first edition held in South Asia.
national.mainsAngle: Explain how circular-economy practices can support prosperity while reducing waste and pressure on resources.

national.headline: VIMARSH 2026 meet brings DRDO and industry together
facts: The Ministry of Defence organised the VIMARSH 2026 DRDO–Industry Synergy Meet in New Delhi on September 15, 2026.
Its theme was “Varta se Vikas.”
The platform connected defence research and development with private industry, MSMEs, startups, academic institutions and manufacturing partners.
Its stated aims included shifting from a buyer–seller model to collaboration across research, design, testing and production, and reducing entry barriers for MSMEs and deep-tech startups.
The meeting sought to strengthen DRDO–industry collaboration and speed development and deployment of indigenous defence technologies.
national.summary: VIMARSH 2026 focused on collaborative development between DRDO and industry, including greater participation by MSMEs and deep-tech startups.
national.staticLink: The meeting concerns the relationship between defence research, industrial production and indigenous technology development.
national.prelimsTakeaway: VIMARSH 2026 was held in New Delhi on September 15 under the theme “Varta se Vikas.”
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how deeper public–private research partnerships can support indigenous defence technology and expand MSME participation.

national.canonicalTopic: Task force examines Formula 1 revival in India
national.headline: Sports Ministry constitutes task force to examine Formula 1 revival
facts: The Union Sports Ministry constituted a 10-member task force on 2026-09-15 to examine the feasibility of reviving Formula 1 in India and developing motorsports.
NITI Aayog Programme Director and Adviser Yugal Kishore Joshi was appointed Chairman.
The task force will examine policies, taxation, infrastructure and partnership models, including tax issues affecting earlier F1 events.
The task force will consider the possibility of an Indian F1 race by 2028.
India last hosted a Formula 1 Grand Prix in 2013 at Buddh International Circuit in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh.
national.summary: A Union Sports Ministry task force was formed to assess a possible Formula 1 return and broader motorsports development in India.
national.staticLink: Formula 1 is governed by the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA); the Indian Grand Prix was held at Buddh International Circuit in 2011, 2012 and 2013.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The task force was chaired by Yugal Kishore Joshi and was to examine the feasibility of an F1 race by 2028.
national.mainsAngle: How taxation, infrastructure and policy frameworks can shape India’s ability to attract international sporting events.

- **Areas to examine:** Policies, taxation, infrastructure and partnership models
- **Taxation:** Includes tax issues affecting earlier F1 events
- **Possibility under consideration:** An Indian F1 race by **2028**

> Exam angle: APPSC may test the task force’s chair, mandate and the status of a possible Indian F1 race.

national.canonicalTopic: India earns medals at 46th Chess Olympiad
national.headline: India takes Open silver and women’s bronze at Chess Olympiad
facts: The 46th Chess Olympiad was held in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, from 2026-09-15 to 2026-09-27, with more than 200 countries participating.
India won silver in the Open section and bronze in the Women’s section.
Uzbekistan won Open gold; Germany took Open bronze. China won women’s gold and Kazakhstan women’s silver.
India won the Nona Gaprindashvili Trophy for best combined performance across the Open and Women’s sections for the third consecutive time.
national.summary: India won medals in both sections of the 46th Chess Olympiad and retained the combined-performance trophy for a third consecutive edition.
national.staticLink: The Chess Olympiad is organised by the International Chess Federation (FIDE).
national.prelimsTakeaway: India earned Open silver, women’s bronze and the Nona Gaprindashvili Trophy in 2026.
national.mainsAngle: India’s international sporting performance and the development of chess as a competitive discipline.

national.headline: Kumik is declared Ladakh’s first Heritage Village
facts: Kumik village in Zanskar was declared Ladakh’s first Heritage Village on September 15, 2026, during the inauguration of the Zanskar Festival–2026.
The village is noted for traditional mud houses, sacred sites, agricultural practices and Tibetan Buddhist traditions.
Kumik preserves Kanjur manuscripts and other Tibetan Buddhist texts; Kanjur is the canonical collection of Buddhist scriptures in the Tibetan Buddhist tradition.
Zanskar is in Kargil district, Ladakh.
national.summary: The Heritage Village recognition highlights Kumik’s built and living cultural heritage, including its traditional architecture and Tibetan Buddhist manuscripts.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Kumik is in Zanskar, Kargil district, Ladakh; its recognition as the region’s first Heritage Village was announced on September 15, 2026.
national.mainsAngle: Consider how heritage recognition can support conservation of architecture, cultural practices and indigenous knowledge.

sources.title: Kumik Declared Ladakh’s First Heritage Village

national.notes:
# 1. Heritage Village recognition
- **What:** **Kumik** declared **Ladakh’s first Heritage Village**
- **Status:** **APPROVED**
- **When:** **September 15, 2026**
- **Occasion:** Inauguration of the **Zanskar Festival–2026**
- **Location:** **Zanskar, Kargil district, Ladakh**
- **AP link:** No direct AP-specific link established
# 2. Heritage features
- **Built heritage:** Traditional mud houses and sacred sites
- **Living heritage:** Agricultural practices and Tibetan Buddhist traditions
- **Manuscripts:** Preservation of **Kanjur** manuscripts and other Tibetan Buddhist texts
- **Kanjur:** Canonical collection of Buddhist scriptures in the Tibetan Buddhist tradition
# 3. Significance
- **Recognition focus:** Kumik’s traditional architecture and living cultural heritage

> Exam angle: APPSC may ask Kumik’s location, its heritage-village status and the festival occasion.
